raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Prevent `AssertionError: Expected a cached item` when a multimodal request exceeds the processor-only LRU capacity. Retain requested payload references before inserting misses, so an earlier insert cannot discard a later hit.

Related #26195. This differs from #34749, which converts cache assertions into request errors without preserving the evicted payload. No open PR implementing request-local processor-only retention was found.

## Claims

- Requests such as `[new C, cached A, cached B]` succeed with a cache that holds only two images.
- Retained tensors, prompt updates, image ordering and repeated-image placeholders match uncached processing exactly.
- Payload lookups use constant-time `LRUCache.peek()`, which leaves eviction order and hit statistics unchanged. No cache-wide dictionary or tensor copies are made.
- Metadata-only and shared-memory sender behavior and the LRU storage budget are preserved.

## Validation

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Tested base `fb7def9ef9`, real LLaVA CPU processor | All three eviction-order regressions fail with `AssertionError: Expected a cached item` |
| Updated branch, CPU | Nine LRU/processor checks and six existing IPC, shared-memory eviction and oversized-item checks pass |
| Preceding head `0cdb70d572a9`, H200 MIG 35GB | The new `RemoteOpenAIServer` regression passed in [Buildkite #98285](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98285#01a187b5-57c0-4e8f-82d1-9427bb7940e1); relevant multimodal jobs also passed in [Buildkite #98389](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98389). Its unrelated P2P failure is fixed by #64555, included in the rebased branch |
| Earlier v0.30.0 Kimi backport, TP8/DCP8/PP2, eight API servers, 8 MiB processor cache | 48/48 cache-pressure responses returned HTTP 200 with correct image order and complete SSE; the original processor reproduced the assertion |
| Earlier Kimi backport with DSpark K=3 and CPU offload | Full endpoint suite passed; accepted speculative-token delta 7,630; both PP pods retained UIDs, readiness and zero restarts |

Fresh full CI: [Buildkite #98475](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98475) is running on rebased head `a5111456ec1a`, based on main `4b47db922b83`. Both patch commits are unchanged after rebase (`git range-diff`); local checks and pre-commit passed again.

The new `peek` test verifies payload identity, stored `None`, missing-key defaults, unchanged hit statistics and eviction of the original oldest entry. It fails with `AttributeError` on the base runtime, which lacks `peek`.

CPU test commands, from a vLLM/test environment:

```sh
env -u UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 VLLM_PLUGINS='' VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts='' \
  tests/utils_/test_cache.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py \
  -k 'lru_cache or processor_cache_preserves_hits_when_request_exceeds_capacity or (processing_correctness and llava-1.5-7b-hf)' -q --tb=short

env -u UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 VLLM_PLUGINS='' VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts='' tests/multimodal/test_cache.py \
  -k 'ipc_enable_disable_consistency or oversized_item_is_served_uncached or cache_eviction_lru_cache or cache_eviction_shm_cache' -q --tb=short
```

Results on rebased head `a5111456ec1a`: `9 passed, 515 deselected`; `6 passed, 24 deselected`. Local execution used an existing uv-managed Python 3.12.11 environment. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy, Ruff, markdownlint and test tethering.

To reproduce the original failure, run the added processor regression against the base runtime:

```sh
env -u UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 VLLM_PLUGINS='' VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts='' \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py::test_processor_cache_preserves_hits_when_request_exceeds_capacity -q --tb=short
```

Base output, for each of the three orders:

```text
vllm/multimodal/cache/base.py:428: in get_and_update_item
    assert mm_item is not None, f"Expected a cached item for {mm_hash=}"
E   AssertionError: Expected a cached item for mm_hash='...'
```

The GPU regression launches real LLaVA weights with two API servers, a two-image cache and prefix caching disabled. It keeps requests on one HTTP connection and compares the pressure request's prompt count and token logprobs with a cold-cache reference. Buildkite selects the processor, utility and endpoint tests and covers their changed source files.

The earlier Kimi endpoint suite covered complete nonempty 512-token SSE, cached prompt logprobs, single/multiple images, tools and roundtrip, code execution, reasoning, long context, French/Arabic, creative output, memory, spatial vision, 80 load requests at concurrency 8/32, and 26 constrained JSON requests plus four ordinary companions. Normal responses were manually inspected and coherent. Neither PP pod logged grammar rejections, engine deaths, CUDA/NCCL errors or tracebacks during those tests. That run validates the original retention backport; the new lookup refinement has not been deployed to Kimi.

### Lookup performance

The previous accessor constructed `_MappingOrderCacheView`, whose `UserDict` constructor copied every cache entry for each requested item. The review refinement replaces this with a direct lookup in the LRU's backing dictionary.

Measured on macOS arm64, Python 3.12.11, cachetools 7.2.6. Times are medians of five samples; each sample performs 20 old lookups or 50,000 `peek` lookups. Temporary allocation is traced separately.

| Cache entries | Previous lookup | `peek` lookup | Previous temporary allocation | `peek` temporary allocation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1,000 | 49.50 µs | 0.039 µs | 39,152 B | 0 B |
| 10,000 | 532.36 µs | 0.037 µs | 311,536 B | 0 B |
| 100,000 | 6,354.41 µs | 0.039 µs | 5,767,408 B | 0 B |

This is a lookup microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput or capacity measurement.

<details>
<summary>Lookup timing reproduction</summary>

```sh
env -u UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER uv --no-config run --no-project --python 3.12 --with cachetools python - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
import statistics
import timeit

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("cache", "vllm/utils/cache.py")
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(module)
for count in (1_000, 10_000, 100_000):
    cache = module.LRUCache(count)
    for index in range(count):
        cache.put(str(index), index)
    key = str(count // 2)
    for name, lookup, number in (
        ("previous", lambda: cache.cache.get(key), 20),
        ("peek", lambda: cache.peek(key), 50_000),
    ):
        samples = timeit.repeat(lookup, number=number, repeat=5)
        print(count, name, statistics.median(samples) / number * 1e6, "us")
PY
```

</details>

## Details

Touching all requested hashes cannot protect every hit when a request's working set exceeds the cache budget. Inserting C can evict A even though A was classified as cached before processing; the merge then supplies `None` for A and asserts.

Snapshot requested local payload references before inserts, using `LRUCache.peek()` without changing eviction order or statistics. If a hit is subsequently evicted, supply the retained tensor/update tuple through the existing insertion path. Sender caches inherit a local lookup returning `None` and keep their existing behavior.

The request-local dictionary and references last through the merge. The LRU remains bounded, but tensors needed by an in-flight request can outlive their cache entries; the optimization guide documents this transient memory. No tensors are copied, and there are no model-runner, scheduler, GPU encoder-cache or speculative-decoding changes.

Earlier Kimi validation used the pinned v0.30.0 image, TP8/DCP8/PP2, DSpark K=3 and eight API servers. CPU offload used 128 GiB/rank and 12,000 eager blocks, with actual PP0/PP1 pools of 69.21/103.82 GiB per rank. Offload behavior is unchanged.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

</details>

detail.title: [Bugfix] Preserve multimodal processor-cache hits during request eviction

files.patch:
@@ -419,6 +419,11 @@ A processed item larger than this budget is served uncached (with a warning)
 instead of failing engine startup; raise `mm_processor_cache_gb` if you want
 those items cached.
 
+With processor-only caching, a request can contain more processed multi-modal
+data than the cache budget. Cached tensors and prompt updates needed by the
+request remain referenced while its inputs are merged, even if they are evicted
+from the LRU. The budget limits cache storage, not transient per-request memory.
+
 If you do not benefit much from the cache, you can disable both IPC
 and processor caching completely via `mm_processor_cache_gb=0`.

@@ -3,20 +3,97 @@
 
 import json
 
+import httpx
 import openai
 import pytest
 import pytest_asyncio
+from PIL import Image
 from transformers import AutoProcessor
 
 from tests.entrypoints.multimodal.conftest import TEST_IMAGE_ASSETS
 from tests.utils import ROCM_EXTRA_ARGS, RemoteOpenAIServer
+from vllm.config import ModelConfig
+from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY
+from vllm.multimodal.cache.base import MultiModalCache
 from vllm.multimodal.media import MediaWithBytes
 from vllm.multimodal.utils import encode_image_url, fetch_image
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
 
 MODEL_NAME = "microsoft/Phi-3.5-vision-instruct"
 MAXIMUM_IMAGES = 2
 
+
+def test_processor_only_cache_eviction_preserves_chat_logprobs():
+    """A later image hit must survive inserts on the same API worker."""
+    model = "llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf"
+    images = [Image.new("RGB", (112, 112), c) for c in ("red", "green", "blue")]
+    processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(
+        ModelConfig(model, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 3})
+    )
+    processed = processor(
+        "<image>" * 3,
+        mm_items=processor.info.parse_mm_data({"image": images}),
+    )
+    items = processed["mm_kwargs"]["image"]
+    capacity = MultiModalCache.get_item_size(items[0]) + MultiModalCache.get_item_size(
+        items[1]
+    )
+    urls = [encode_image_url(image) for image in images]
+    args = [
+        "--api-server-count",
+        "2",
+        "--mm-processor-cache-gb",
+        str(capacity / (1 << 30)),
+        "--limit-mm-per-prompt",
+        '{"image": 3}',
+        "--max-model-len",
+        "4096",
+        "--max-num-seqs",
+        "1",
+        "--no-enable-prefix-caching",
+        "--enforce-eager",
+    ]
+    # Keep all requests on one API worker, whose cache holds exactly two images.
+    limits = httpx.Limits(max_connections=1, max_keepalive_connections=1)
+    with (
+        RemoteOpenAIServer(model, args) as server,
+        server.get_client(http_client=httpx.Client(limits=limits)) as client,
+    ):
+
+        def complete(order):
+            return client.chat.completions.create(
+                model=model,
+                temperature=0,
+                max_tokens=1,
+                logprobs=True,
+                top_logprobs=5,
+                messages=[
+                    {
+                        "role": "user",
+                        "content": [
+                            {"type": "text", "text": "Describe these images."},
+                            *[
+                                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": urls[i]}}
+                                for i in order
+                            ],
+                        ],
+                    }
+                ],
+            )
+
+        expected = complete((2, 0, 1))
+        complete((0, 1))
+        actual = complete((2, 0, 1))
+        assert actual.usage.prompt_tokens == expected.usage.prompt_tokens
+        assert actual.choices[0].message.content
+        expected_probs = expected.choices[0].logprobs.content[0].top_logprobs
+        actual_probs = actual.choices[0].logprobs.content[0].top_logprobs
+        assert [p.token for p in actual_probs] == [p.token for p in expected_probs]
+        assert [p.logprob for p in actual_probs] == pytest.approx(
+            [p.logprob for p in expected_probs], abs=1e-3
+        )
+
+
 # Required terms for beam search validation
 # Each entry is a list of term groups - ALL groups must match
 # Each group is a list of alternatives - at least ONE term in the group must appear

@@ -26,6 +26,7 @@
 from vllm.inputs import MultiModalDataDict, MultiModalInput
 from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY
 from vllm.multimodal.cache import MultiModalProcessorOnlyCache
+from vllm.multimodal.cache.base import MultiModalCache
 from vllm.multimodal.inputs import MultiModalFeatureSpec, batched_tensors_equal
 from vllm.multimodal.processing import BaseMultiModalProcessor, InputProcessingContext
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
@@ -296,6 +297,38 @@ def random_vision_chunk(
     return {"type": "video_chunk", "video_chunk": video_array}

From Codex:

- [P2] Each payload lookup copies the entire cache — base.py:429. self._cache.cache constructs _MappingOrderCacheView, whose UserDict constructor copies all cache entries. Since _merge_mm_kwargs calls this for every requested item, merging M items now costs O(M × cache entries), including ordinary cache hits. A local synthetic measurement showed approximately 1.3 ms per lookup at 10,000 entries and 17 ms at 100,000 entries. Add a constant-time, non-mutating LRUCache.peek() method and use it here.

Thanks @DarkLight1337 for catching this, could you take another look please?

Addressed in 6bcac54bb132fd1623f9ce0c77c4719f0b3e3e66. `get_cached_item()` now uses a constant-time `LRUCache.peek()` that reads the backing dictionary without copying entries, touching eviction order or updating hit statistics.

Added a regression for payload identity, stored `None`, miss defaults, unchanged stats and eviction of the original oldest entry. The local lookup benchmark at 100,000 entries changed from 6.35 ms and 5.77 MB of temporary allocation to about 0.039 µs and no measured temporary allocation (five timing samples; not a serving throughput benchmark).
